newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent slips after big gains, stays under $20.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent slips after big gains, stays under $20.

text.p: IPE Brent futures eased lower in early trading in a reaction to gains of nearly $2 a barrel over the past five trading sessions.
June Brent was down six cents at $19.66 at 0928 GMT having dipped to $17.87 a week ago.
Technical analysts said the market was likely to stay pinned in the $19.50 to $20 a barrel range on Tuesday and dealers saw little impact from the physical market.
In Nigeria five oil flow stations, with a production of 120,000 barrels per day (bpd), have been shut because of tribal fighting.
But no force majeure has been declared and exports are continuing normally, said Shell.
Oil dealers said they still expect thin loading programmes at North Sea fields in June with around 24 cargoes less than full output.
Also underpinning the market was a sharp rise in U.S. gasoline prices on Monday that some dealers believe could suck up to 300,000 tonnes of material from Europe during May.
But the bottom of the barrel, heavy fuel oil, remains sluggish and could keep refinery margins under pressure.
Meanwhile, in Scotland, a blockade by fishing boats of the Sullom Voe oil ports continued but the fishermen said they would move when presented with legal documents supporting an order to move.
Also, there has been a further delay in BP's North Sea oil field which is now not expected to start pumping oil before late August.
Meanwhile, in Texas, a fire at CITGO's 150,000 barrel per day refinery was still burning after an explosion on Monday, according to police.
IPE gas oil was down 25 cents at $173.50 a tonne for June. Dealers said premiums for physical Rotterdam barges were steady at about $1 a tonne above the screen.
Technical support and resistance for June gas oil was seen at $172.25 to $175.25 by brokers MeesPierson Derivatives in London.
